text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Both ruling and opposition parties in Macedonia have a positive opinion of the American SECI initiative on cooperation of southeastern European countries. Opposition asks the government for more information from the government on this initative and its significance for Macedonia.

- Macedonian Foreign Minister Ljubomir Frckoski will take part at the traditional international breakfast in the White House at the beginning of February. This is an opportunity for Macedonia to establish new contacts and relations with influential politicians and businessmen from over the world.
- Thirteen deputies from ethnic Albanian PDPA and NDP parties will not participate in the work of the parliament because none of their demands have been considered, discussed or accepted.
- IMPRO-DPMNY demands revision of the financial transactions in municipalities where they are in power following local elections. Most of municipality coffers empty.

- Head of the World Bank mission to Macedonia Helen Goldstein said Monday that the bank is satisfied with results Macedonia has achieved in the stabilisation of the economy. The World Bank is to approve a new four-year $50 million loan to Macedonia.
